title: IFFI opens in Goa with Pawlikowski's 'Fatherland'; Sawant announces plan for film city
dek: The nine-day festival is showing more than 150 films from 86 countries. The Indian Panorama began on Saturday, and Uttam Kumar's centenary is among the tributes.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
The 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI) opened in Goa on Friday night with Paweł Pawlikowski's Fatherland, and Goa's Chief Minister, Pramod Sawant, used the ceremony to announce plans for a film city in the state with production, post-production, visual effects and film-education facilities.

The festival, which runs until 28 November under the theme "Stories Without Borders", received more than 1,900 submissions from 137 countries and will show more than 150 films from 86 countries, according to reports. On Saturday, its first full day, the programme moved to the screens in Panaji, Porvorim, Margao and Ponda, with a masterclass marking 50 years of the Kannada filmmaker Girish Kasaravalli and the first screenings of the Indian Panorama.

## The opening night

The ceremony was held at the Dr Shyama Prasad Mukherjee Stadium near Panaji. A symphonic orchestra led by the three-time Grammy winner Ricky Kej performed "A World of Cinema Through Music" before the opening film.

Mr Sawant said IFFI had been part of Goa's cultural calendar for more than 22 years. "Cinema allows us to experience different cultures and find the common ground that unites us," he said, according to reports. He cited the Goa Film Shooting Act of 2021, an online single-window clearance system and financial aid for filmmakers as steps to make the state a filmmaking hub, and urged young Goans to make films. He did not give a cost or timeline for the film city.

Chanchal Kumar, secretary of the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting, called the festival "a meeting place of cultures, ideas, memories and human experiences". The festival director, Ashutosh Gowariker, said: "Borders are not merely lines drawn on maps. They are also our habits we build around ourselves."

The juries were introduced on stage: the International Competition jury, chaired by the director Aanand L. Rai, with Bogdan Mureșanu, Sol Berruezo Pichon-Rivière, María Alejandra Rojas and Ratchapoom Boonbunchachoke; and the Indian Panorama juries, chaired by Madhur Bhandarkar for features and Himansu Sekhar Khatua for non-features.

## The films

Fatherland, by the Polish director of Ida and Cold War, shared the best director prize at the Cannes Film Festival this year, according to reports. The mid-festival film is I Matter and the closing film is We Are All Strangers.

The Indian Panorama, 76 films in 18 languages, opened on Saturday with Dhurandhar, alongside the feature Thaai Kizhavi and the non-feature film Becoming, and the Goan film Ancessao was also screened. Free open-air screenings began at 7 pm on Saturday at Miramar and Vagator beaches and at Ravindra Bhavan in Margao, with Natsamrat, Bombilwaddi and the animated film The Wild Robot.

## Bengal at the festival

The festival is marking the birth centenary of Uttam Kumar, the leading man of Bengali cinema for nearly three decades, along with those of the filmmakers Shakti Samanta and Raj Khosla, the actors Suryakant Mandhare, Prem Nazir and Raj Kumar, and the composers O.P. Nayyar and Ravi, the ministry has said. The Indian Panorama includes the Bengali feature Pagla Ghora, directed by Sekhar Das, and Mr Khatua, who chairs the non-feature jury, is a former director of Kolkata's Satyajit Ray Film and Television Institute.

## What happens next

The International Competition winners, including the Golden Peacock for best film, will be announced at the closing ceremony on 28 November. Masterclasses and panels run at the Kala Academy in Panaji until 27 November, and the WAVES Film Bazaar, the festival's market for buyers and producers, marks its 20th year.
